title: Week 11 Mastery Quiz · Civil Society, Interest Groups, and Social Movements

questions.question: An association reports 5,000 members but only 70 attended its public hearing. What inference is warranted?
options: Association membership automatically measures active participation in every campaign.
Membership and hearing participation are distinct measures of mobilization
The 70 hearing attendees can be treated as a random sample of all members.
The hearing attendance count alone establishes whether advocacy changed public policy.
questions.explanation: Membership and hearing participation are distinct measures of mobilization

questions.question: A fictional labor union organizes across several regions but its petition lists duplicate signatures. What should the researcher verify?
options: Whether the union has a logo
Whether its leaders are famous
Unique signatories, collection methods, and independent records before reporting support
Only the petition's length
questions.explanation: Unique signatories, collection methods, and independent records before reporting support

questions.question: Two advocacy groups support the same law; one uses court litigation and the other public marches. Which comparison best identifies strategy?
options: Resources, political opportunity, institutional access, and expected mechanisms of influence
Only the groups' founding years
The weather on one rally day
The names of their websites
questions.explanation: Resources, political opportunity, institutional access, and expected mechanisms of influence

questions.question: A government permits assembly in law but imposes indefinite permit delays on critics. Which question follows?
options: Whether the law uses enough words
Whether every rally is peaceful
How many officials wrote the rule
Whether administrative practices restrict meaningful exercise of assembly rights
questions.explanation: Whether administrative practices restrict meaningful exercise of assembly rights

questions.question: A social movement grows rapidly after a policy announcement. Which evidence is needed before claiming the announcement caused growth?
options: Only its website traffic
Membership trends, prior organizing, rival explanations, and a plausible mechanism
A photograph of a crowd
One leader's prediction
questions.explanation: Membership trends, prior organizing, rival explanations, and a plausible mechanism

questions.question: Fictional coalition: environmental and worker groups agree on emissions reductions but disagree on job protections. What should the student examine?
options: Only their shared slogan
Which group has older offices
Policy tradeoffs, affected populations, negotiation terms, and evidence of likely effects
Only the number of meetings
questions.explanation: Policy tradeoffs, affected populations, negotiation terms, and evidence of likely effects

questions.question: A report describes one protest as 'violent' without specifying incidents or sources. What response demonstrates source criticism?
options: Verify incident evidence, attribution, chronology, and whether characterization applies to all participants
Repeat the adjective as fact
Ignore all eyewitness reports
Assume every protest is identical
questions.explanation: Verify incident evidence, attribution, chronology, and whether characterization applies to all participants

questions.question: An interest group donates to campaigns and later receives favorable policy. What is the defensible causal claim?
options: The donation conclusively bought the policy
No relationship can ever be investigated
Every donor received a benefit
Association prompts investigation of timelines, decision records, alternative explanations, and legal standards
questions.explanation: Association prompts investigation of timelines, decision records, alternative explanations, and legal standards

questions.question: A religious charity provides food relief and advocates legal change. Which distinction is analytically useful?
options: Service delivery proves electoral control
Civil-society organizations can combine direct services with policy advocacy; assess each role separately
All charity is a political party
The organization has no public impact
questions.explanation: Civil-society organizations can combine direct services with policy advocacy; assess each role separately

questions.question: A fictional municipal consultation receives responses only in one language in a multilingual region. Which participation issue arises?
options: None if responses are voluntary
The region's population is irrelevant
Language access may exclude affected communities and distort claims of public consent
One-language responses prove unanimous approval
questions.explanation: Language access may exclude affected communities and distort claims of public consent

shortResponse: How do people organize outside government to influence law, culture, institutions, and public priorities?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
